rows.selection_reason: With zero completed experiments, the most critical uncertainty is establishing a performance floor for the RNA modality alone, which serves as the reference against which all multimodal, multiprofile, and learned-encoder choices will be judged. config_022 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible RNA baseline: a well-understood linear encoder (PCA), no multi-profile aggregation, no image branch, and no fusion step. This isolates the raw signal quality of the RNA data with minimal confounding from learned representations or architectural complexity. It directly tests whether a basic RNA-only model achieves competitive accuracy, which is essential before investing budget in more complex multimodal or multiprofile variants. Under a limited budget, anchoring the search with a clean, interpretable baseline is the highest-information first step: it calibrates expectations, reveals whether the task is already solvable with simple features, and provides a clear ablation target for every subsequent experiment.

The only completed experiment (config_022) is a minimal RNA-only baseline (pca_n2000, singleprofile, no aggregation) achieving ~48.5% accuracy. The largest unresolved uncertainty is whether adding the image modality provides any benefit at all. Config_002 is the cleanest test of this question: it keeps the RNA encoder (pca_n2000), profile setting (singleprofile), and aggregation (None) identical to config_022, and introduces only the image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) with the simplest fusion (concat). This isolates the effect of adding image information. If accuracy improves substantially, it justifies further investment in multimodal designs and lets us then probe encoder choice, fusion strategy, and profile/aggregation settings. If it does not improve, it strongly suggests the image modality (at least with this RNA representation) is not contributing, redirecting the budget toward RNA-encoder or profile-setting experiments. Under a limited budget, resolving this fundamental modality question before exploring more complex interactions is the highest-information next step.

Evidence: config_022 (RNA-only, PCA, single) achieved 0.485 acc and config_002 (multimodal, PCA, ViT-L, concat, single) achieved 0.535 acc, confirming that adding an image modality with PCA RNA helps. However, we have no information on whether the RNA encoder choice matters—PCA is a simple linear baseline, and a learned representation like scgpt could capture nonlinear biological structure. Question: config_004 changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scgpt while holding everything else identical to config_002 (multimodal, singleprofile, imagenet_vit_l, concat fusion). This is a clean single-variable A/B comparison that isolates the RNA representation effect. Why best next: With only 2 experiments done, the RNA encoder is the largest untested design axis that could substantially shift performance. A clean comparison to config_002 will tell us whether learned RNA encoders are worth pursuing, directly guiding whether subsequent experiments should focus on scgpt/scvi variants or whether PCA suffices. This maximizes information gain per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: config_002 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, concat) achieved the best accuracy (0.5353), substantially outperforming both the RNA-only baseline (config_022, 0.4849) and the scgpt variant (config_004, 0.4348). This strongly suggests pca_n2000 is the superior RNA encoder and that adding the image modality via concat provides a meaningful gain. However, fusion strategy has only been tested as 'concat' so far. Question: config_005 is identical to config_002 except fusion changes from concat to weighted, cleanly isolating the effect of fusion strategy while holding RNA encoder, image encoder, and profile setting constant. Why this is best: With only 3 completed experiments, the evidence base is sparse. This single-variable comparison directly extends our best result and answers whether a more sophisticated fusion (weighted) can further improve on the promising pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l combination. If weighted fusion helps, it opens a high-value direction; if not, we confirm concat is sufficient and can redirect budget toward profile/aggregation questions. It avoids changing multiple factors simultaneously and is the most information-dense next step.

Evidence: Our best result (config_002, acc=0.5353) uses multimodal + pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + concat in singleprofile mode. All four completed experiments are singleprofile, so the effect of multiprofile (and its required aggregation step) is completely unexplored. This is the largest remaining uncertainty in the design space. Question: Does moving from singleprofile to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation improve performance when all other settings (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, concat) are held at their known-best values? Why this experiment: config_021 is the minimal, clean extension of our best configuration—changing only the profile setting (and its coupled aggregation), which isolates the multiprofile/aggregation effect. If it outperforms config_002, it validates the added complexity and justifies further exploration of aggregation types (transformer) and other encoders in the multiprofile regime. If it underperforms, it tells us singleprofile is sufficient and we can focus budget on image-encoder or RNA-encoder variations within singleprofile. Either outcome substantially reduces uncertainty about a major design axis under a limited budget.

Evidence: The largest performance jump so far came from moving singleprofile→multiprofile (config_002: 0.535 → config_021: 0.629), and the current best (config_021) uses avgpool aggregation. We have no multiprofile data with transformer aggregation, leaving open whether a more expressive aggregation could further improve over simple averaging. Question: config_038 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) is identical to config_021 except aggregation changes from avgpool to transformer, cleanly isolating the effect of aggregation strategy. Why best next experiment: It is a single-variable ablation on the most promising configuration, directly testing whether the multiprofile gain can be amplified by learned aggregation. If transformer aggregation helps, it opens a rich sub-space (configs 045, 035, 036, etc.); if it does not, it confirms avgpool is sufficient and we can redirect budget toward RNA encoder or image encoder variations in the multiprofile setting. This is more informative than testing fusion (concat≈weighted already shown in singleprofile) or switching encoders (higher risk of confounding).

Evidence: The largest performance jump (0.535→0.629) came from switching to multiprofile+avgpool, and the current best (config_021) is multimodal. However, we have no rna_only multiprofile baseline, so we cannot decompose how much of the 0.629 is driven by multi-profile RNA aggregation versus the image modality. Question: config_032 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) directly isolates the RNA multiprofile contribution. It enables two clean comparisons: (1) vs config_022 (rna_only, singleprofile, 0.485) to measure the multiprofile gain for RNA alone, and (2) vs config_021 (multimodal, multiprofile, 0.629) to quantify the image's marginal contribution in the multiprofile regime. Why best under budget: A single experiment yields two critical decompositions, reducing uncertainty about whether the image encoder is a major performance driver or a minor add-on. This determines whether future budget should prioritize image-encoder variants (e.g., resnet50) or RNA-side improvements (e.g., scvi_n200), making it the highest-information-per-experiment choice.

Evidence: config_021 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) is the current best at 0.629 acc. In singleprofile, concat (0.535) and weighted (0.532) fusion were nearly equivalent, but we have no multiprofile data on weighted fusion. Question: Does weighted fusion interact differently with multiprofile avgpool aggregation than concat does? This is a single-variable change from the current best, isolating the fusion mechanism. Rationale: Under a limited budget, testing one design axis at a time from the best-known configuration is the most efficient way to determine whether a simple swap can improve performance or confirm that concat is already optimal in this regime. If weighted fusion matches or exceeds concat, it opens a new axis (e.g., combining with alternative RNA encoders); if it underperforms, we can rule out weighted fusion and focus remaining budget on other untested dimensions (e.g., image encoder or RNA encoder in multiprofile).

Evidence: The current best configuration (config_014: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted; acc=0.635) establishes that multiprofile + avgpool + weighted fusion is a strong pipeline. However, the RNA encoder choice remains the largest untested uncertainty: PCA_n2000 works well, scGPT performed poorly (0.435 vs 0.535 in single-profile), but scvi_n200 (a 200-dim VAE latent) is a fundamentally different learned representation that has not been tested. Question: config_030 changes only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 while holding all other settings at their best-known values (multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted), providing a clean single-variable comparison against config_014. Why best: Under a limited budget, resolving whether a learned RNA encoder can match or beat PCA in the best-known pipeline is the highest-information next step. If scvi_n200 improves on PCA, it opens a new optimization axis; if it does not, we confirm PCA as the robust choice and can redirect effort toward the image encoder or other dimensions. This avoids the risk of changing multiple variables and directly extends the strongest evidence we have.

The current best (config_030: scvi_n200, vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieved 0.7062 acc. With pca_n200, avgpool clearly outperformed transformer (0.6352 vs 0.5988, ~3.6 pp gap), but scvi_n200 produces a fundamentally different, richer latent representation that may interact with aggregation differently. Config_007 changes only aggregation (avgpool→transformer) while holding scvi_n200, vit_l, multiprofile, and weighted fusion constant, giving a clean single-variable test of whether transformer aggregation could exploit the richer scvi embeddings. This is the highest-impact remaining uncertainty: if transformer matches or beats avgpool here, it opens a new architectural direction; if not, we can confidently lock in avgpool and redirect budget to other axes (e.g., image encoder). It is a logical exploitation of the best configuration while still resolving a key design question.
